findings.issue: No browser or HTTP check of the new /team page, the disabled 'Team is full' button state, or the new CSS — only the Playwright acceptance suite validated rendering
findings.suggestion: For UI-adding changes, start the dev server and eyeball the new page (or capture a screenshot) even when tests pass

findings.issue: Two failing probes into app/node_modules before confirming the directory didn't exist

findings.issue: Malformed read tool call (passed 'command'/'offset' instead of 'path')
findings.suggestion: Match the tool's parameter schema; the immediate bash fallback was the right recovery

summary: A near-model single-pass session: requirements, tests and the framework's installed source were all read up front, the one architectural decision (cookie-backed SSR team state to avoid a hydration flash) was made correctly and early, and the feature landed with zero fix cycles — 63/63 tests plus build and typecheck all green on the first run. Weaknesses are minor: four trivially failed tool calls and no visual/browser inspection of the new UI beyond the automated suite. I'd point to this trace as an example of how to work in an unfamiliar framework.
